projects.title: Flexible Work and Wellbeing

primary.coverage: American Time Use Survey Well-Being Module public microdata; selected years listed by BLS
primary.licence_or_access: US federal public data; verify current reuse notice before redistribution

teaching_sample.reason: Small fixed panel generated for a transparent classroom exercise; it is not an extract of a respondent-level survey.

cleaning: restrict to employed respondents in a documented source extract
construct remote-days measure and survey weights if using ATUS
drop/flag impossible scores; never infer causal assignment
for sample: parse numeric fields and create worker/month fixed-effect dummies

formulae.FE: wellbeing_it = alpha_i + tau_t + beta*remote_days_it + gamma*workload_it + e_it

projects.expected_result: The fixed synthetic sample is designed to yield a positive within-worker remote-days association after workload control; it is a calculation check, not evidence of a population effect.
chart_suggestions: coefficient plot for OLS and FE with confidence intervals
remote-days versus wellbeing scatter colored by worker
projects.causal_limit: Neither selection-adjusted OLS nor fixed effects remove time-varying confounding, reverse causality, or non-random workplace adoption; do not make a causal claim without a credible design.

projects.title: Restaurant Demand and Food Waste

primary.coverage: Loss-adjusted food availability documentation and aggregate data
primary.licence_or_access: US government public data; data are aggregate and not restaurant transactions

secondary.licence_or_access: FAO terms apply; link is used for context, not copied microdata

teaching_sample.reason: A reproducible fictional point-of-sale exercise, necessary because public restaurant transaction-level data with waste observations are not reliably available as a common open benchmark.

cleaning: remove cancelled service days only with pre-declared rule
separate avoidable waste from safe donation/compost where data exist
projects.expected_result: For cost=5, price=12 and salvage=1, critical ratio=7/11≈0.636; an order near the 63.6th demand percentile maximizes one-period expected profit under the stated distribution.
chart_suggestions: profit and waste by order quantity
projects.causal_limit: Aggregate food-loss statistics cannot identify a restaurant's demand process or the causal effect of insurance on waste.

projects.title: Oil Prices and Inflation

oil.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis / source noted on series
oil.coverage: daily Europe Brent Spot Price FOB, USD per barrel
oil.licence_or_access: FRED provides free access; retain source attribution and check series notes

inflation.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis / US Bureau of Labor Statistics
inflation.coverage: monthly Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, seasonally adjusted, index 1982-84=100
inflation.licence_or_access: FRED provides free access; retain source attribution and check series notes

teaching_sample.reason: Fixed illustrative monthly series with deliberately documented values; use the cited FRED download for observed updates rather than treating the sample as history.

cleaning: download raw series with date/value columns and archive retrieval date
resample daily oil price to monthly mean before merging with monthly CPI
compute log change; align lags without look-ahead
document revision vintage; use percent changes rather than index levels for a simple teaching regression

formulae.distributed_lag: inflation_t = alpha + b0*oil_change_t + b1*oil_change_t-1 + gamma*output_gap_t + e_t

projects.expected_result: The synthetic sample is constructed for a positive contemporaneous-plus-one-month oil association. It must not be interpreted as an identified structural pass-through estimate.
chart_suggestions: scatter of lagged oil change and inflation
projects.causal_limit: Oil moves with global demand, supply disruptions, exchange rates and monetary policy; small time-series OLS has confounding, autocorrelation and revision risks.

validation: every teaching sample carries a status label
all sources have URLs and access notes
formula variables resolve to variable dictionaries
no synthetic sample is labelled observed
